 Manchester City’s feud with the Premier League following the guilty verdict will dominate their season, but it is now events on the pitch that are proving a genuine concern.
 Enzo Maresca has lost three league games in a row and, at the City Ground, there was further evidence of defensive instability, strange team selection and key players underperforming.
 Eight games without a clean sheet underlines their vulnerability and Maresca has much to ponder over the international break with his team six points behind leaders Arsenal.
 What a response from Nottingham Forest to Oliver Glasner’s brutal “no-compromises” rant last weekend, as the home team secured only the second league win in front of their own supporters this year.
 It was a former City player, Liam Delap, who tormented them with two brilliant individual goals to give Glasner what he hopes will finally be lift-off.
 "The day that Delap ARRIVES" 🤩
Nottingham Forest regain their two-goal lead! https://t.co/5yk5eIhPhe
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 Forest’s £50m record signing was on the 55-man list for Thomas Tuchel’s latest England squad and more performances like this will enhance his chances of senior recognition. It was the archetypal “No 9” performance.
 While Forest will hope this proves a turning point in their season, these are certainly worrying times for City.
 Marc Guéhi and Josko Gvardiol are both badly out of form and were replaced at half-time with injuries, while it was another alarming evening for goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma .
 Despite a brief rally early in the second half, City never looked capable of ending their slump. Even the sight of Manchester United in the bottom three will have done little to cheer their supporters.
 Maresca said: “I’m always concerned, even when we win games. We won seven in a row and we have now lost three, so over the break we need to understand what we can do better.
 “When you lose a game you want to play again immediately, but this break is also good for the players. We are going to use it to clarify how to improve things. The defeats have all been different and we will look at them.”
 Enzo Maresca has pledged to fix City’s problems during the international break
 Credit : Getty Images/Neal Simpson
 Forest’s home results have been poor for some time, but this was their best performance under Glasner, with the club’s owner Evangelos Marinakis making his first appearance of the season.
 Glasner has frequently highlighted Forest’s poor running data in recent weeks, but their heat maps here will have been electrifying. Forest outran City by six kilometres.
 When Delap thundered in the third goal, Glasner ran up the touchline to celebrate with his players at the corner flag.
 After calling out his squad last weekend following the defeat at Brentford, the response of the players here was always going to be telling.
 Glasner said: “I think everybody felt huge happiness but also relief, to be honest. I could see a team today that was fighting for each other. The energy in the team and at the City Ground was incredible.
 “We know exactly what Liam’s strengths are when he can use his power and his finishing with right and left is just amazing.
 “There are a lot of things to improve, he’s still a young man in only his second regular Premier League season. The strike with his left foot is something you either have or you don’t have.”
 Forest had started brightly and it was their Brazilian international, Jair Cunha, who finally ended their wait of 8½ hours for a home goal.
 It was another City mistake, with Gvardiol dispossessed by Cunha after a poor touch, with the defender advancing into the area to slot his shot into the corner.
 Jair Cunha BRILLIANTLY slots home his first goal for Nottingham Forest to give them the lead against Manchester City! 💥 https://t.co/HcP4txscTK
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 Forest increased their lead in the 18th minute with a fine goal from Delap. Taking the ball from within his own half, Delap raced to the City area before thumping a shot past Donnarumma.
 "His first home goal for Forest is a CRACKER!"
Liam Delap doubles Nottingham Forest's lead 🔴 https://t.co/pr75p7lfVZ
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 City’s defending was again abysmal, with Guéhi and captain Rúben Dias allowing Delap to run unchallenged for more than 50 yards.
 It was the earliest City have been two goals behind in a league game since November 2019 against Liverpool (13 minutes).
 Guéhi and Gvardiol were both hooked at half-time and it did provoke a response from the visitors. Rayan Cherki produced the first snarl of defiance seven minutes into the half with a sublime half volley which flew into the top corner.
 "A THUNDERBOLT to fire Manchester City back into it!"
Rayan Cherki has got a goal back for Manchester City 💥 https://t.co/ZBDVPvElVC
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 Forest were momentarily wobbling and City scented blood, attacking from the flanks and dominating possession.
 Yet Forest did recover their composure with a deflected shot from Ryan Yates looping over Donnarumma and striking the top of the crossbar.
 Delap then delivered another missile after a quick counter-attack, firing the ball into the top right corner and in off the post with his left foot. Glasner was up the touchline, celebrating with his players at the corner flag, and will be hoping he finally has lift-off.
 Oliver Glasner SPRINTED down the touchline to join in the team celebrations after Liam Delap's goal 🔥 https://t.co/oFCAPWMlNF
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 As time ticked away, with the mist rolling in from the River Trent, Forest’s supporters chanted: “Can we play you every week?”
 Latest updates

 at the City Ground.

 8:15PM
 More from Maresca on the goals City conceded
 Link copied to clipboard 
 First half when you don’t match intensity and lose all the duels it’s difficult. Then when we want to react, it’s too late.
 In this kind of match, you need to match intensity and win duels, otherwise it’s always complicated. First half we were not good enough in terms of duels, second balls - we lost all of them. Then when we went to react we were 2-0 down and in football that is always complicated.
 The first goal we are trying to play, build. The second one we lost duels in the middle of the pitch then the third one we lost the duel at the edge of their box. We need to match intensity in these kind of games.
 Enzo Maresca conceded his team were second best in the first half
 Credit : PA/Nigel French
 8:08PM
 Maresca reacts
 Link copied to clipboard 
 I’m always concerned, even when we win games. We won seven in a row and we have now lost three so over the break we need to understand what we can do better.
 We are going to use it to clarify how to improve things. The defeats have all been different and we will look at them.
 We were not good enough in the first half and couldn’t match their intensity.
 8:05PM
 Glasner on Delap
 Link copied to clipboard 
 We knew exactly his strengths when he can use his power and his finish with right and left is just amazing. A lot of things to improve, he’s still a young man in, I would say, his second regular Premier League season.
 Maybe it is his third but he didn’t play so often last year. Today no single player deserves to be mentioned because I thought it was such a team effort. We waited for our situations and how passionately we defended our goal in the box, I could mention everyone.
 8:05PM
 Glasner saltues Forest’s performance
 Link copied to clipboard 
 It was a very good day to play Manchester City but, to be honest, today, the energy in the team and at the City Ground was so incredible that it would have been tough for every team in the world to play against us today.
 So all the credit to the players and our fans for this amazing Saturday evening.
 It’s not about me or my standards, it’s about our standards. I could see a team today that was fighting for each other. Every single player left his heart on the pitch and, of course, we could see after the goal early in the second half, the quality and the pressure.
 When it was tough we had our fans, who backed up and supported us. Also the new players. We knew there would be times to suffer and bring in the new players to continue this hard work.
 A fantastic night and, I think, a deserved win.
 7:35PM
 Not a great day for Manchester

 7:30PM
 Liam Delap speaking on the pitch
 Link copied to clipboard 
 It’s been coming, we’ve been performing like that every week just not putting the ball in the net.
 We did everything right, got the three points and now we can enjoy the international break.
 I just wanted to run and shoot, and luckily it went.
 It gave us a little breathing room [the third going]. It’s always tough playing City, you’re running after them for 90 minutes so we knew it was going to be a battle.
 It was a perfect ball from Morgan [Gibbs-White], he’s set up a lot this season that we’ve not been able to convert so thankfully we could put it in the net.
 Liam Delap scored his first home goals for Forest
 Credit : PA/Nigel French
 7:26PM
 FT: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest’s first home Premier League win of the season is one for the scrapbook, especially for Liam Delap who scored with two corking finishes. Glasner’s team have been knocking on the door, and finally a game turned in their favour to help them climb out of the relegation zone.
 Three straight league defeats for City, who now trail Arsenal by six points (they go to the Emirates later this month). They made a terrible start to the game, and only played well for the first 20 minutes of the second half.
 Brighton can go second on their own tomorrow and Manchester United will start the day in the relegation zone.
 Man City’s defensive frailties were in evidence again
 Credit : Reuters/Andrew Boyers
 7:21PM
 90 minutes: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 City still trying to prise Forest open, but some belief has drained out of them. Ndiaye slaloms through a few challenges, before a Foden shot from the edge of the box is blocked. Just four minutes of stoppage time to play.
 7:17PM
 86 minutes: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 The ball bounces back off Doku and out for a Forest goal kick, and the home fans can see the finish line now. Sangare then wins a booming tackle on O’Reilly. Glasner makes another change: Liam Delap receives a standing ovation, replaced by Igor Jesus. Even Marinakis broke into applause.
 7:13PM
 83 minutes: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Superb hold-up play from Liam Delap, making it stick and winning a free-kick on the far touchline. The City Ground rises to salute him. Man of the match will be an easy decision.
 7:11PM
 80 minutes: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Phil Foden on now for City, replacing Enzo Fernandez who departs to a chorus of boos. Still time and enough quality on the pitch for City to salvage something, but you wonder if there chance has gone. Gibbs-White does well to help Forest keep the ball inside City’s half.
 7:08PM
 77 minutes: Forest 3 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 City straight back down the other end trying to retrieve the situation and avoid a third successive league defeat but Sels claims a corner. Forest need to avoid conceding in the next five minutes. Fernandez has been fouled in a central position, around 35 yards out.
 Glasner channeled his inner-Mourinho after Delap’s goal.
 Oliver Glasner SPRINTED down the touchline to join in the team celebrations after Liam Delap's goal 🔥 https://t.co/oFCAPWMlNF
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 7:06PM
 GOOOAALL! Delap does it again
 Link copied to clipboard 
 This goal might be even better than his first, an outstanding counter-attacking strike. Delap started the move by holding the ball up and turning out of pressure in his own half, laying the ball off for Gibbs-White who carried the ball forward.
 Gibbs-White had runners either side, but went left to Delap. The angle was against the striker, but he unleashed a left-footed shot across Donnarumma that cannoned off the inside of the far post and in.
 "The day that Delap ARRIVES" 🤩
Nottingham Forest regain their two-goal lead! https://t.co/5yk5eIhPhe

 7:03PM
 72 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest behind the ball and defending in numbers, they have at least avoided being cut open down the flanks. City continue to pile the pressure on though, and it takes some manful last-ditch defending to repel the crosses.
 6:59PM
 68 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest are growing into the game again now, and Yates’ shot from distance deflects and loops over a stranded Donnarumma and clips the top of the bar. City break from the resulting corner, with Ndiaye barreling up the pitch with a fantastic run, and he is dragged down by Ndoye at the expense of a booking.
 6:57PM
 65 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Confirmation of that Forest double sub: Netz and Ndoye replace Munoz and McAtee. That means Neco Williams to right wing-back, a measure aimed at trying to contain Doku which is a difficult task.
 6:55PM
 63 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Crucial header from Cunha with Haaland lurking behind at the back post. But the waves of City attacks continue, Glasner is preparing a couple of substitutions because Forest cannot get out at the moment.
 The Forest fans then scream for a Kusanov foul on Delap, but before McAtee is penalised for a forceful challenge on Andersonb.
 VAR checks and concludes that a yellow card is sufficient punishment.
 6:51PM
 60 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest struggling to cope in both wing-back positions at the moment, City’s rotations causing all manner manner of problems. This time it was O’Reilly in behind, and from the corner Sels flaps off the line. Feels a matter of when not if City score their second.
 6:49PM
 58 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 City players complaining about Sels taking too long over a goal kick, hoping for a corner, but the referee did not heed their calls. Chance of a break for Gibbs-White but he left the ball behind and Anderson mopped up.
 6:48PM
 56 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Nunes misjudges a long ball forward towards Delap, but O’Reilly chests back his cross to Donnarumma.
 Then City scythe through Forest down their right with Nunes and Ndiaye surging forward, and Haaland curled not far over the bar with a right-footed strike. A matter of inches away.
 6:45PM
 55 minutes: Forest 2 City 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest scrambling now, City causing them all manner of problems through Doku down the left. Cherki has come to life since his goal, bringing out all of his tricks and flicks.
 6:43PM
 GOOAALL! Cherki fires City back into it
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Doku drifts of the back of Munoz too easily, and his cross flicks off Yates in the middle and drops for Cherki to crack home a peach of a half-volley. First time from the edge of the box, it flew past Sels. Cherki has struggled, but he can always produce those moments of brilliance.
 "A THUNDERBOLT to fire Manchester City back into it!"
Rayan Cherki has got a goal back for Manchester City 💥 https://t.co/ZBDVPvElVC
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 6:42PM
 51 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 McAtee heads down Gibbs-White’s cross hoping for Delap to hang back but the striker had run ahead of the ball.
 6:39PM
 49 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Liam Delap penalised for a push on Kusanov, but before that Forest’s defence mopped up well when City tried to find Haaland with early service. 
 Then Ndiay and Nunes combine well down the right, but Cunha heads the cross away before Cherki passes the ball straight of play.
 6:37PM
 47 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 O’Reilly has a great relationship with Doku down City’s left so that is something Forest need to be waray of.
 Cherki with a cute pass from inside his own penalty area to find Ndiaye, and City begin to monopolise the ball inside Forest’s half.
 6:36PM
 We are back under way
 Link copied to clipboard 
 City get the secon half started.
 6:35PM
 Double sub on the way from Maresca
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly replace Guehi and Gvardiol. So Kusanov moves to centre-back alongside Dias, and O’Reilly is on at left-back.
 6:26PM
 Blitzed
 Link copied to clipboard 
 2 - Liam Delap's goal for Nottingham Forest (18th min) makes it the earliest Manchester City have been two goals behind in a Premier League game since November 2019 against Liverpool (13th min). 
Shocked. https://t.co/my8jjWqVIl
— OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) November 7, 2026 
 6:26PM
 John’s half-time verdict
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Manchester City are heading for a third successive league defeat unless there is a drastic improvement in the second half.
 They have looked defensively unstable again and are being pressed out of possession by a Forest team full of confidence.
 Oliver Glasner has frequently highlighted Forest’s poor running data but in the first-half here their heat maps will have been electrified. 
 6:21PM
 HT: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 A brilliant home performance from Forest, excelling in and out of possession. City have been too easily exposed in transition again, and the likes of Guehi and Donnarumma just look plain out of form. Better from Enzo Maresca’s team in the last five or 10 minutes of the half, but they have a mountain to climb against one of the league’s best defences.
 Nottingham Forest pounced on City’s errors
 Credit : Reuters/Andrew Boyers
 6:18PM
 45 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Just the two minutes of added time to play and City have a corner, but the delivery was too deep for Haaland to do anything with. Just one more minute for Forest to negotiate.
 6:17PM
 44 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Long spell of City possession in Forest’s half, this has been their best spell of the match as half-time approaches but McAtee defends well against Doku. Dias just about puts enough on his pass back to Donnarumma with Delap lurking.
 City then win a free-kick in the Forest half, Williams catching Fernandez late.
 6:15PM
 42 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Cunha with a goal-line clearance to deny Haaland and City! It was a really incisive through ball from Anderson to release Haaland, and City’s striker rounded Sels but could not squeeze the ball beyond Cunha from a tight angle. From the corner, Anderson flicks the ball up and volleys on the turn, but the shot is straight at Sels.
 6:12PM
 40 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 The Forest fans are on Ndiaye’s case, believing that he is indulging in amateur dramatics, claiming he was elbowed by Murillo. It was more of a light scrape with the hand. Certainly no force or violence in it.
 6:09PM
 37 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Milenkovic heads a cross behind and City have a corner. Very unconvincing from Sels, trying to pat away the delivery while claiming he was being fouled by Guehi, but Forest get away with it.
 Then McAtee pounces on a bouncing ball in front of Anderson, and is tripped by his former team-mate.
 6:07PM
 35 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Great work again form James McAtee, carrying the ball down the right touchline and winning a throw-in off Anderson. Gvardiol clears Munoz’s launched delivery. Reaching half-time with a clean sheet will be Glasner’s objective from here.
 6:05PM
 32 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Haaland with his first shot of the game, but it was an ambitious attempt on the volley, running away from goal to latch on to Guehi’s chipped pass over the top. The striker hit the target, but not enough power to trouble Sels.
 6:03PM
 29 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 He could change the game with a shot or pass in an instant, but Cherki has struggled so far. Loose with the ball, and City’s midfield balance with him and Enzo Fernandez in there will again be questioned. Diligent work from Ndiaye to track back and defend against Gibbs-White.
 5:59PM
 26 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Enzo Fernandez has just missed City’s best chance of the game, header over the bar from around six yards. Marc Guehi with the right-footed, inswinging delivery. As things stand, Manchester United are in the relegation zone.
 Forest crunch into another tackle in midfield, and Delap wins a free-kick. They have been fantastic to a man so far.
 Enzo Fernandez heads over the bar
 Credit : PA/Nigel French
 5:55PM
 23 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Now Forest have a corner after a teasing Munoz cross. The home team are rampant. Their underlying numbers suggested they were performing like a team closer to the top of the league and they have looked just that so far. From the corner, a snap shot by Murillo is straight at Donnarumma.
 5:53PM
 20 minutes: Forest 2 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 James McAtee fires over the bar from the edge of the area when completely unmarked! City all over the place at the moment, Forest are setting traps and they are walking straight into them.
 5:51PM
 GOOOAALLL! That is more like it from Liam Delap
 Link copied to clipboard 
 His first goal at the City Ground in a Forest, and what a finish it is.
 City made a mess of a loose ball in midfield with Anderson and Ndiaye going all “after you Claude”, and Delap was straight at the heart of their defence again.
 You would not know he has been struggling in front of goal, because Delap shifted the ball out of his feet a drilled a powerful shot beyond Donnarumma high into the net.
 What a goal from Liam Delap.
 It can be revealed that Forest’s record signing was on the 55-man list for Thomas Tuchel’s latest England squad, but did not make the cut.
 He has been discussed as a potential heir for Harry Kane and goals like that will certainly strengthen his case.
 "His first home goal for Forest is a CRACKER!"
Liam Delap doubles Nottingham Forest's lead 🔴 https://t.co/pr75p7lfVZ
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 5:48PM
 16 minutes: Forest 1 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Donnarumma was nowhere to be seen on the corner, flapping at fresh air. No Forest player was there to apply the finish at the back post. That hint of defensive instability at City remains.
 Chants of “you’re going down with United” and “you’re going down with the Derby’ from the Forest fans.
 5:47PM
 14 minutes: Forest 1 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Good defending from Williams up against Ndiaye but Doku helps City keep the squeeze on. 
 Things break down with a careless Cherki pass in the middle of the pitch, and Forest break down their right through Delap and Munoz. 
 Forest’s striker did not look at all sure of himself, and is grateful for a corner.
 5:44PM
 11 minutes: Forest 1 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Milenkovic with more good defending, this time intercepting a Cherki flick around the corner, before Forest do well to keep possession. A stretching run in behind by Delap prompts Dias to cover across and concede a throw in City’s half.
 The Forest found themselves an open City defence again after Gibbs-White picked up the scraps off Delap, but McAtee did neither one thing nor the other, and Donnarumma claimed.
 5:41PM
 9 minutes: Forest 1 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Crucial block by Milenkovic to deny Doku after a sweeping City move, the left-winger was teed up by a clever pull-back by Ndiaye from the right. Great start to the game, it is set up perfectly now.
 5:39PM
 GOOOAALL! Cunha punishes Gvardiol
 Link copied to clipboard 
 What a start for Forest, they have finally scored a home goal this season as the clock ticks past five minutes. It was really slack from Gvardiol, dallying on the ball and drifting aimlessly infield. Cunha picked his pocket and the defender carried the ball towards the box. He had passing options left and right, but kept his head while unopposed and rolled the ball beyond Donnarumma with his left foot.
 Forest have scored their first goal at the City Ground since the final game of last season. That is a drought of almost eight and a half hours.
 Jair Cunha BRILLIANTLY slots home his first goal for Nottingham Forest to give them the lead against Manchester City! 💥 https://t.co/HcP4txscTK
— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 7, 2026 
 5:35PM
 2 minutes: Forest 0 City 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Bright start from the home team. James McAtee with some neat close control, before Delap drifts in behind Gvardiol. A long Forest through flicks off the head of Cunha and into the gloves of Donnarumma.
 City then establish some possession, with Gvardiol advanced and playing inside Doku in a narrow position.
 5:32PM
 KICK OFF!
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Forest get the game under way.
 Evangelos Marinakis, the Forest owner, is at the City Ground today in his first appearance of the season.
 Marinakis has been busy with his various other business interests but is here this evening. 
 As a very superstitious man, can his return bring Forest some good fortune?
 5:28PM
 The teams are out at the City Ground
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Just like the lyrics of Forest’s Mull of Kintyre -inspired pre-match song, there really is a mist rolling in from the Trent on a crisp autumnal evening.
 Remembrance Day will be marked just before kick-off.
 5:27PM
 The state of play with City
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Even a City win today will have them three points behind Arsenal for the international break.
 The margins for error are very small in title races and who knows how damaging those two successive league defeats could be for Enzo Maresca.
 There is, of course, their feud with the Premier League over the guilty verdict for breaking financial rules which could render everything irrelevant. 
 It really is a poor situation for both City and the governing body. The whole season feels phoney and paralysed with uncertainty.
 5:19PM
 Anderson back at the City Ground
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Very warm reception for Elliot Anderson from the Forest fans as he runs to the tunnel leading to the dressing rooms.
 Anderson was at Forest for two seasons before that £116m move to Manchester City.
 5:11PM
 City defensively vulnerable

 Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.
 Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.
 The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.
 “I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”
 Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.
 City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.
 Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.
